t: Listen to a talk in an agriculture class.
Two methods of farming are often compared.
In conventional farming, a single crop is planted across a large field year after year.
This approach is efficient for harvesting machines, but it drains the same nutrients from the soil every season, so farmers must add more and more fertilizer.
Crop rotation, in contrast, changes what is grown in a field from one year to the next.
For example, a farmer might plant corn one year and beans the next.
Beans return nitrogen to the soil, so the following crop needs less fertilizer.
Crop rotation does have drawbacks, though.
Farmers have to learn how to grow and sell several different crops, and in the first few years their income can be less predictable.
